title: review: G2b: repo map generator — orchestrator repomap writes memory/architecture.md (module, public symbols, one-line purpose, commit sha) under about 1,000 tokens, refreshed after every merge
spec:
memory/architecture.md is empty (the record.sh set architecture path exists but nothing generates content). The analysis asks for an aider-style repo map: selected symbols and signatures within a token budget, versioned against repository state, retrieved by workers instead of rediscovered.
Change:
1. New orchestrator/repomap.py: build(root, budget_chars=4000) parses every orchestrator/*.py with ast, takes the module docstring's first sentence, top-level classes and functions with their signatures (name and parameter names, no bodies), ranks modules by how many other modules import them (simple import graph) and trims the lowest-ranked symbols first until the budget fits; output is markdown: a header line 'repo map <sha> <date>' then one section per module with the symbol list; deterministic ordering.
2. cli.py: `orchestrator repomap [--budget N] [--stdout]` writes .orchestrator/memory/architecture.md (or prints).
3. merge.py: after a successful fast-forward, regenerate architecture.md in the ORCH_ROOT checkout only when the merged diff touched orchestrator/*.py (cheap check via git diff --name-only), never failing the merge if generation raises (log to stderr).
4. Tests in tests/test_repomap.py: test_build_fits_budget (a fixture package with three modules, one importing the other two, budget forces trimming and keeps the most-imported module), test_build_deterministic, test_header_has_sha; tests/test_merge.py::test_merge_refreshes_repomap_on_py_change (monkeypatched build called once).
Note: do not let the generator import the modules; ast only.
acceptance: uv run orchestrator repomap --stdout on this repo prints under 4,000 characters and lists daemon.py, bus.py and spawn.py with their public functions
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree

comments.issue: Budget-trim loop sorts candidates by (rank, module_name, symbol) and pops from the front, so it strips every symbol from one module completely (in rank-then-alphabetical order) before touching the next module at the same rank, instead of spreading cuts evenly. Verified by running `uv run orchestrator repomap --stdout` on this repo: output is 3913 chars (under budget) and bus.py's functions survive, but daemon.py (rank 3) and spawn.py (rank 7) sections show only their module docstring with zero `- def ...` lines — every symbol below bus/pool's rank was wiped out first. This directly fails acceptance criterion 3, which requires daemon.py, bus.py and spawn.py to all show their public functions. The 3-module test fixture (ranks 0 vs 1, one symbol per module) is too small to expose this uneven-stripping behavior.

`if not os.environ.get(IN_TESTS_GREEN):` guards the entire tests-green.sh invocation. This is needed so a nested self-hosting test run (pytest inheriting gate_env from the outer subprocess.run call) doesn't recursively re-invoke the real gate script — but the same check means any process that has ORCH_TESTS_GREEN set in its own environment for any other reason (leaked env var, unrelated tooling, future bug) will silently skip the test gate entirely and fast-forward the merge with unverified code. This is the one hard safety property the module's docstring promises ('rebase -> tests-green -> fast-forward') and the house rule 'tests-green.sh exits 0 is the merge bar' depends on. An explicit parameter threaded through nested calls would be safer than an ambient, generically-named env var controlling a security-critical gate.
